    StartersVerdell's baconThick bacon baked crisp, with maple syrup on the sideHow to make it12 rashers of thick cut bacon100ml maple syrupLay the bacon on a rack over a tray.Bake at 200°C until crisp.Cut into pieces and serve warm with a small bowl of maple syrup for dipping.Café breakfast bitesToast squares topped with scrambled egg, crisp bacon and chivesHow to make it4 rashers of bacon6 eggs40g butter6 slices of white bread1 bunch chivesFry the bacon until crisp and chop.Scramble the eggs softly in butter.Toast the bread, cut into small squares and top each with egg, bacon and snipped chives.Road trip pretzel chicken tendersThe road trip to Baltimore with Simon and CarolHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken tenderloins crumbed in crushed pretzels and baked crunchy, with a honey mustard dip, packed in a box for the car.Heat the oven to 210°C.Crush 150g salted pretzels to coarse crumbs.Toss 600g chicken tenderloins in 40g plain flour, then 2 beaten eggs, then the pretzel crumbs, pressing to coat.Lay on a lined, oiled tray, spray with oil and bake 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.Mix 80g Dijon mustard, 3 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp mayo for dipping.Potato latkes with sour cream and applesauceSell crazy someplace else. We're all stocked up.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsBaltimore crab cakesPan-fried crab cakes with Dijon, spring onion and crisp breadcrumbsHow to make it500g crab meat3 tbsp mayonnaise1 tbsp Dijon mustard3 spring onions100g breadcrumbs2 tbsp vegetable oil1 lemon1 bag mixed salad leavesMix the crab with the mayonnaise, Dijon, sliced spring onion and breadcrumbs. Shape into 8 cakes.Chill for at least 30 minutes.Pan fry in the vegetable oil until golden on both sides.Serve with lemon and a green salad.Café meatloaf with brown sugar glazeThe New York café where Carol waits tablesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef meatloaf with onion, garlic and herbs, baked under a sticky tomato and brown sugar glaze, sliced thick with buttery mash and minted peas.Heat the oven to 180°C.Mix 1kg beef mince, 1 grated onion, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 80g breadcrumbs, 2 eggs, 80ml milk, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tsp salt.Shape into a loaf in a lined tray.Mix 80ml tomato sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tbsp cider vinegar and spread over.Bake 1 hour, rest 10 minutes and slice.Serve with 1kg potatoes mashed with butter and milk, and 400g peas boiled with mint.SweetsCafé banana cream pieBiscuit crust, vanilla custard, sliced banana and whipped creamHow to make it250g plain sweet biscuits110g butter, melted600ml full cream milk4 egg yolks100g caster sugar50g cornflour1 tsp vanilla extract3 bananas300ml thickened creamCrush the biscuits with the melted butter and press into a pie dish.Cook the milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour until thick, add the vanilla and cool.Layer sliced bananas in the crust and spread over the custard.Top with whipped cream.Chill for the setting time.DrinksCafé coffee milkshakeStrong chilled coffee blended with vanilla ice cream and milkHow to make it250ml strong coffee500g vanilla ice cream250ml milk1 tbsp caster sugar150ml thickened cream1 tbsp cocoa powderBrew the coffee and chill it for at least an hour.Blend the coffee with the ice cream, milk and sugar until thick and smooth.Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses. Whip the cream to soft peaks, spoon on top and dust with cocoa.Manhattan Special espresso sodaYou make me want to be a better man.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
